content.text: {"quote_faithful": "yes", "verdict": "confirmed", "evidence_kind": "invalid_inference", "fatal": "yes", "explanation": "The quote is verbatim from Claim 3.2. The notation \u03c0(s) is defined only for finite prime sets, and the premises given (T meets every t \u2208 C, hence every supp(a_i)) do not force T to be finite; the text nowhere proves that minimal transversals of C are finite. The objector's family C={{2,x_n}} shows an intersecting antichain of finite sets can have an infinite minimal transversal {x_n : n\u22651} (deleting x_k leaves {2,x_k} unhit), so finiteness is not automatic from (i)+(ii). Hence hypothesis (iii) of the Step 4 Theorem is verified only for finite minimal transversals. This is load-bearing: in Step 4(c) the transversal I \u222a Z_\u03c9 is infinite and Zorn yields a possibly infinite minimal T, whose membership in C (and finiteness, used in 'Since T is finite...') is exactly what is unproved. The finiteness obligation therefore fails as written."}
